newsitem.title: USA: Good probability of ongoing low inflation-Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Good probability of ongoing low inflation-Rubin.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Friday the probability was good for continuing low inflation.

"You've always got to be watchful with respect to inflation but I think everything that I see suggests to me the probability is very high that inflation will remain at low levels as far as I'm comfortable looking in the future," Rubin told reporters on Capitol Hill.
Rubin cautioned that tax legislation currently being drafted on Capitol Hill should guard against exploding the budget deficit in later years.

But he said he would not prejudge the legislation until he saw it. House Ways and Means Chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, has said he hopes to complete writing the tax bill over the weekend so his committee can consider it next week.
Congressional leaders and the White House reached agreement last month on a budget outline that called for $85 billion in net tax cuts over five years and $250 billion net tax cuts over 10 years.

Asked if President Clinton would oppose a tax bill that the administration's analysis showed would increase the budget deficit after 10 years, Rubin replied: "Well, I don't think this is the time to talk about opposing bills. I think we're a little bit early in the process, and the president wants to sign tax legislation."
Rubin added: "But one of the things he (Clinton) is very focused on is not having exactly what you just said, which is a tax bill that threatens the remarkable accomplishments of deficit reduction."
